sections.heading: Overview
content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has directed providers to use modifier CT to report computed tomography (CT) services furnished on equipment that is not consistent with dose optimization standards established by the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA). Enforcement of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013, also known as the MITA Smart Dose standard, for the Medicare Program is required by the Protecting Access to Medicare Act of 2014. The criteria of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013 ensure use of the lowest radiation dose necessary to get the image quality needed by providers to make a proper diagnosis. The standard outlines four attributes CT equipment should meet to ensure that a patient receives the highest standard of care as established by professional societies and regulatory agencies. Performing CT services on equipment that meets all elements of the standard helps reduce a patient’s lifetime exposure to potentially cancer-causing medical radiation. Humana works to reduce our members’ exposure to medical radiation. Directly and through vendor partnerships, we educate our members on the risks of medical radiation exposure and encourage our in-network providers to provide high quality advanced diagnostic services that meet a broad set of industry standards, including NEMA Standard XR 29-2013. This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for services reported with modifier CT .

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires providers to follow the appropriate Medicare Program guidance for correct coding using modifier CT . Providers must report modifier CT with procedure codes for applicable CT services performed on equipment that does not meet all four attributes of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013. Humana reduces reimbursement for the technical component ( TC) of an applicable CT service reported with modifier CT by five percent for dates of service in 2016 and by 15 percent for dates of service beginning January 1, 2017. Note: Pre-authorization requirements may apply when applicable CT services are provided to a Humana member.

sections.heading: Definitions of Italicized Terms
content: • Applicable CT services : Computed tomography services identified by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) as subject to the modifier CT payment reduction rule. • Modifier CT : Computed tomography services furnished using equipment that does not meet each of the attributes of the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA) XR-29-2013 standard. • Technical component (TC) : The technical component of a service is for all non-physician work and includes administrative, personnel and capital (equipment and facility) costs and related malpractice expenses. Modifier TC is used with the billing code to indicate that the TC is being billed.
